# Open SGP4XP outliers for side A (amendment 7 input)

Side B: closed-modules task branch task/modules-sdn-gp-propagator-20261023 at 03388d3 and later (dist 61d4ec4e6a12),
the SPEC of closed-modules main 7f83efa (amendments 1-6). Conformance E2E (`test/conformance.e2e.mjs`, corpus seed
20261023: 10,200 SGP4XP sets, 8 times each over 7 days) against side A's oracle (USSF Sgp4Prop 9.9, black box): 80974
samples, outputs SHA-256 72dcf60050464606b1aaddb63ed121f965845a957d05adcb4c4f06ccc8a7bedc. A sample is open when it differs by more than 1 m and no inherent
class accepts it: decay (within 1e-4 of the drag displacement of a decaying or heavy-drag set), or shadow (inside the
envelope of the module run twice with every rounding-limited SPEC 4 decision of every rate evaluation taken one way,
then the other: amendment 6's (a), a candidate with 1e-13 <= |S| <= 1e-11, and (b), a decision that moving a, e, i,
Omega, omega or a Sun-direction component by 8 units in the last place changes). A set is named by its index in the
SGP4XP corpus (NORAD number 40000 plus the index); the element sets are given in full.

| Regime | Decay-accepted | Shadow-accepted | Open samples | Open sets | Worst open (m) |
| --- | --: | --: | --: | --: | --: |
| LEO | 63 | 2 | 62 | 19 | 12.7 |
| SSO | 0 | 1 | 61 | 16 | 3.6 |
| MEO | 0 | 58 | 138 | 44 | 26.9 |
| GEO | 0 | 235 | 283 | 78 | 35.2 |
| HEO | 7 | 15 | 88 | 20 | 622.8 |
| VDS | 0 | 64 | 67 | 22 | 116.0 |

## Findings

- Rounding-limited sets. Each open set was run again with its mean anomaly moved by 1e-12, -1e-12 and 2e-12 deg
  (column *moved*: the largest difference from the oracle on an hourly grid over 7 days, for 0 and the three moves).
  Where that spread exceeds a quarter of the largest, the set is marked *limited*: its outcome rests on shadow decisions
  at the rounding limit in integrator stages, in mixed directions that the two-way envelope does not bracket. GEO 75 of
  its 78 open sets are limited, VDS 15 of 22, MEO 2 of 44; LEO, SSO and HEO none.
- VDS 1805 (116 m, 43.9 m before amendment 6): limited. Amendment 6's 1e-20 kg/m^3 above 2500 km changes the state by
  about 1e-15 and flips a stage decision: with the density 0 there it is 68 m on the hourly grid, with 1e-20 181 m, and
  with the mean anomaly moved by 1e-12 deg 87 to 189 m. Neither outcome is a model error.
- 4.9 against the amendment-6 envelope: of the 163 geometries where the module's decision differs from the library's,
  162 are rounding-limited (both outcomes conform), among them the three where the module's |S| is 0 (sets 1839, 7251,
  5091: limited by (b)). One is not: set 275 at the geometry where the module's candidate has |S| = 5.0e-11 and the
  library takes a sunlit arc.
- LEO, SSO and HEO open sets are stable under the moves: in the module's arithmetic their differences are deterministic
  (HEO 4780 623 m, LEO 2364 12.7 m, SSO 6685 3.6 m). For HEO, 4.10 places 7 node steps at one stage decision each that
  the library's fused arithmetic takes the other way; the two-way envelope flips every limited decision of a run
  together and so does not reproduce one flip alone.
